thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: CRITICAL: gateway error-rate alert (5xx) triggered in us-west-2 - sustained 5xx > 3% over 2m. Paging @lucy (oncall)

lucy (oncall): I'm awake, on it. pulling recent gateway logs and upstream status.

nate (sre): past 5min shows a mix of 502s and 504s coming from model-router cluster - a handful of model-backend pods restarted repeatedly. attaching snippet: 
```
[2026-11-03T11:10:12Z] route=/v1/chat upstream=model-backend-7 status=502 msg="write tcp: connection reset by peer"
[2026-11-03T11:11:03Z] route=/v1/chat upstream=model-backend-2 status=504 msg="deadline exceeded"
[2026-11-03T11:11:35Z] route=/v1/embed upstream=model-router-1 status=502 msg="recv: broken pipe"
```

rachel (infra): I see pod churn on model-backend pool in us-west-2. kube reports OOMKilled 2/5 pods in the last 6m. metrics show increased batch sizes from client X.

lucy (oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) add temporary traffic steering away from us-west-2 for non-Dedicated traffic, 2) enable route-level circuit-breaker at gateway for model-router to fail fast and reduce queueing, 3) apply a target rate-limit for clients exceeding threshold. Which should I do first?

nate (sre): let's steer traffic first to stop user-facing noise while infra fixes nodes. also add an annotation to make sure Dedicated tenants pinned to us-west-2 are excluded from steering. I'm happy to toggle circuit-breaker after the shift.

ops-bot: action: route-weight-adjust executed by lucy (run_id=evt-20261103-211). new weights: us-west-2=25%, us-east-1=75%.

lucy (oncall): applied split 25/75. monitoring panels: error-rate dropped from 3.8% -> 1.1% within 90s. p95 latency increased by ~85ms for affected requests.

tom (product): flagging customer comms. please annotate impacted region and expected latency regression. any SLA impact?

rachel (infra): scaling warm-pool and cordoning a node that OOM'd. also adding temporary pod anti-affinity to reduce co-location. we'll restart the problematic instances in a controlled rolling manner.

nate (sre): observed the 5xx root cause: unthrottled large-batch requests from a small set of clients caused excessive memory usage in model-backend; that cascaded into router timeouts. Proposed post-incident actions:
- Change alert: require 3m sustained window at >2% for global gateway 5xx (was 60s >0.5%).
- Add per-region alerting (by(region)) so a single-region failure doesn't page global oncall.
- Add an alert that fires only when error-rate is spread across many upstream hosts vs single-host failures (to reduce noise).
- Create a synthetic test that sends large-prompt traffic to warm-pool every hour.
- Implement per-client batch-size/read quota at model-acceptor.

lucy (oncall): +1 to all. I'm opening INC-20261103-7 with summary and customer impact: partial elevated 5xx in us-west-2 for ~11 minutes; mitigated by traffic steering and infra scaling; estimated 0.9% of global requests affected, concentrated on few clients.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident INC-20261103-7 created and assigned to eng-sre.

nate (sre): drafting alert change PR: https://git.internal/redwood/alerts/pulls/448 - includes updated prometheus expr and grouping by region. snippet to be applied: 
```
alert: gateway_5xx_sustained
expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="gateway",status=~"5.."}[3m]))
  / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="gateway"}[3m])) > 0.02
for: 3m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/gateway/5xx
  note: "group by region to avoid global pages for single-region incidents"
```

lucy (oncall): we should also add a helper metric: fraction_of_upstreams_with_errors > 0.2 over 5m to differentiate broad outages vs single-host blips. that will reduce noisy pages when one backend misbehaves.

rachel (infra): I'll add a Grafana panel that shows upstream error-hotspots by instance id + memory pressure. dashboard link (temporary): https://grafana.redwood/d/alerts/model-backend-hotspots

tom (product): I'll prepare a short status page message: "We observed elevated errors in us-west-2 and shifted traffic to fallback region; latency may be slightly higher for requests routed to fallback. No Dedicated customers are impacted." posting draft to #status-drafts.

nate (sre): also updating runbook to include circuit-breaker cookbook and exact terraform module we can flip for canary testing. will add the per-client throttling RFC to backlog.

lucy (oncall): handoff to day team: oncall->nate at 09:00 PT. current status: traffic split in place, infra restart in progress, error-rate trending down to baseline. escalate if gateway 5xx >2.5% sustained 5m or if Dedicated tenant reports failures.

nate (sre): taking handoff. staying on for next 60m to verify node restarts.

ops-bot: :memo: Follow-ups added to INC-20261103-7: alert tuning, dashboard creation, runbook updates, throttling RFC.

lucy (oncall): final quick note — applied temporary client throttle for the top offending token (token id xyz) at 5 rps. helped reduce stress on model-backend. will keep until quota enforcement PR lands.

rachel (infra): nodes restarted, warm-pool +3, memory pressure dropping. will monitor for a full 2 hours before resolving.

nate (sre): after-action items assigned. changing alert windows will reduce wake-up noise; tests will exercise the large-prompt path so we don't regress.

tom (product): thanks team. I'll keep comms team looped.

lucy (oncall): incident resolved (mitigations in place, infra healthy). summary: ~11 minutes of elevated errors in us-west-2, ~0.9% global request impact, mitigated by traffic steering and throttles. closing incident if stable for 2h. :white_check_mark:
